## Canopy in brief

- What it is: a layer above Git (not a Git replacement) for repositories where many AI coding agents work in parallel, each in its own worktree.
- What it does: records what each agent reads and writes via harness hooks; notifies an agent in its next tool call when another agent changes a function it read or calls; lets `main` move only through `canopy land`, which runs sandboxed checks on the exact merge commit and attaches an Ed25519-signed record as a Git note; a `pre-receive` hook refuses any other route into `main`.
- Works with: Claude Code (HTTP hooks, the tested path); a Codex adapter and a hook-less `canopy checkin` are on the main branch (Codex adapter not yet run against Codex). Node 22.13+, Git 2.38+, no npm dependencies. macOS tested; Linux sandbox untested.
- Status: version 0.3.0, on npm as `canopy-land` (the command is `canopy`; plain `canopy` on npm is a different package). 0.2 adds users and tokens, owners and approvals, per-folder model rules, a tighten-only manager agent, OSV.dev dependency checks, environments (staging, production), Slack/Discord/webhook notifications and a catch-up digest. 0.3 adds contracts: the author of a breaking change to shared code must publish a test that fails on the old code before landing, and callers are shown the new signature and that test. 174 tests pass, 1 skipped, with scripted agents. Four short trials with real Sonnet agents ({{github}}/canopy/blob/main/docs/TRIALS.md): main passed in 18 of 18 states under Canopy, plain Git broke it in 1 of 4; warned agents adapted mid-task in 1 of 8 cases. Not yet security-tested by a third party and not yet run at length with real agents.
- Measured: hook round trip p50 0.46 ms; semantic conflict reported 22 ms after the edit; about 0.6 s fixed cost per landing; default setting is slower than a plain serial merge queue for unrelated branches (12.2 s vs 9.2 s for eight), `disjoint` setting is faster (5.9 s).
- Try it: `npx canopy-land demo`
- Install: `npm install -g canopy-land`, then `canopy init` and `canopy serve` in your repository. npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/canopy-land
